title: Chart Forge Chart
description: A playable rhythm-game chart: the notes a human author decided to place, and the timing information needed to play them back. This is the Editor's output and the Player's input. A Chart Note is a gameplay object and is a different concept from an Analysis Event, which is an observation about the audio. A chart never contains analysis data. All time values are in seconds from the start of the audio unless stated otherwise. The core model is game-neutral; anything specific to a particular game belongs under 'extensions'.

version.description: Version of the Chart document format (semantic versioning).

metadata.description: Descriptive information about the chart and the song it belongs to.

name.description: Open vocabulary label such as debut, regular, pro, master.

level.description: Numeric difficulty rating, if the target game uses one.

audio.description: The audio this chart is played against. Referenced, never embedded.

timing.description: How chart time relates to audio time and to musical time. A Player needs only 'offsetSec' and note times to play the chart; the tempo information exists so an Editor can draw a beat grid and so patterns can be expressed musically.

offsetSec.description: Time in the audio at which musical time zero (bar 1, beat 1) occurs. May be negative if the first downbeat precedes the audio.

bpmChanges.description: Tempo changes in ascending time order. The chart's tempo is the base 'bpm' until the first change.

beatsPerBar.description: Base time signature numerator, used for the beat grid.

playfield.description: The geometry the notes are placed on. Kept explicit rather than implied by a game name, so that the generic model stays independent of any particular game.

laneCount.description: Number of lanes. Lane indices in notes run from 0 to laneCount - 1, left to right.

profile.description: Name of the gameplay profile this chart targets. 'generic' uses only the core model. Any other value implies a matching entry under 'extensions' and must not change the meaning of core fields.

notes.description: The notes of the chart, in ascending 'timeSec' order.

connections.description: Links between notes that are played as one run. Optional and additive: a chart without it is a chart of independent notes, and a reader that ignores it sees exactly that - every note still has its own time, lane and direction, and is still playable on its own. Each link names two notes by id; no note is altered by being linked.

extensions.description: Namespace for game-specific data, keyed by profile name (for example an object under the key 'deresute'). The core model above must remain meaningful when every extension is ignored, and a Player that does not understand an extension must still be able to play the chart.

id.description: Identifier unique within this document. Stable across edits so that other documents can refer to a note.

timeSec.description: Time in seconds from the start of the audio.

direction.description: A swipe direction, as one of the eight compass points.

noteEndAction.description: What the player does at the end of a note that has one, when it is something other than simply releasing. Absent means an ordinary release. Deliberately its own object rather than a reuse of the note's 'direction': on a hold or a slide, 'direction' would be ambiguous about whether it described the start or the end, and this says plainly that it is the end. An object rather than a bare string so other end actions can be added later without another shape change.

type.description: The kind of end action. Open vocabulary, like chartNote.type; a Player that meets an unknown one should report it rather than guess.

direction.description: Swipe direction, for an end action that has one.

slideWaypoint.description: One intermediate judgement point of a slide: a moment the player must have reached, and the lane they must have reached it in. A waypoint is an instant, not a duration; a slide is judged at its points and travelled between them.

timeSec.description: When this point of the slide must be reached.

lane.description: Lane this point is in, 0-based from the left, less than playfield.laneCount.

chartConnection.description: A link between two notes that are played as one run, such as a sequence of flicks swiped through in a single motion. Both notes keep their own id, time, lane and direction; this only says they are joined. It carries no judgement of its own - nothing happens on the link itself, only at the notes it joins.

type.description: What kind of run this link belongs to. Open vocabulary, like chartNote.type; a Player that meets an unknown one should report it rather than guess.

toNoteId.description: The later note. Must be strictly after 'fromNoteId' in time, which is what keeps a run a run and makes a loop unrepresentable.

type.description: Gameplay kind of the note. 'tap' is a single hit; 'hold' is held from 'timeSec' to 'endTimeSec'; 'flick' is a directional swipe; 'slide' is a chain of judgement points travelled between lanes, using 'waypoints' and 'endLane'. Open vocabulary; a Player that meets an unknown type should report it rather than guess.

timeSec.description: When the note must be hit.

lane.description: Lane the note starts in, 0-based from the left, less than playfield.laneCount.

endTimeSec.description: When a held note is released, or when a slide reaches its last point. Required in practice for 'hold'; absent for instantaneous notes, and absent for a slide point that has not been joined to another. Must be greater than 'timeSec'.

endLane.description: Lane the note ends in, when it moves across lanes.

endAction.description: What happens at 'endTimeSec', when it is something other than an ordinary release - a Long or a Slide that finishes with a flick, for example. Only meaningful on a note that has an end. Optional and additive: a reader that ignores it still sees a correct note that simply releases at the end.

waypoints.description: Intermediate judgement points of a multi-point slide, between 'timeSec'/'lane' and 'endTimeSec'/'endLane', in strictly ascending time order. Only meaningful on a slide. Optional and additive: a reader that ignores it still sees a valid slide with the correct start and end, which is the documented fallback.

direction.description: Swipe direction for directional notes such as flicks.

sourceEventId.description: Optional provenance: the id of the Analysis Event the author was looking at when placing this note. It is a human-authored back-reference for tooling and re-analysis, never a claim that the note was generated from the event, and a Player must ignore it.

metadata.description: Author or tool specific extra data. A Player must be able to play the note while ignoring this.
